cells.tense: The hands are already working on the small thing they keep returning to.
cells.act: release what is done and keep what is not
cells.ask: Take the thing you're tending and look at what it's become. One part of it has reached its end — set that part down, leave the rest growing under your hands, and let the week pass without adding anything to it.
cells.core:
You learn by your hands. You take up a thing, stay with it, and find out how it grows by watching what you did last time and what it did back. That is the whole apprenticeship, and it is working — this moment before anything is chosen isn't empty for you; it's a workbench with something alive on it.

What feeds you next is finishing. When one part is complete, the release arrives with it, and it lands as completion rather than loss. So this week, look at what you're tending and say plainly which part is finished, and bring that part to its end. Keep the rest. Nothing is being given up here; something is being closed by the one who knows it best.
cells.sheetLine: You can say which part is done and close that part.
cells.verb: Tending something into the form it is learning to take
cells.place: In the open moment before anything has been chosen

cells.tense: The form it should take is being settled long before anything is touched.
cells.act: sense what has not happened yet, with wonder
cells.ask: Sit with one unfinished thing and picture what it could become — no plan, no fix, nothing to carry out afterward. Stay with it as long as it holds your attention, then get up and go on with the day as it was.
cells.core:
Care has become speed. Everything you touch gets its whole future decided first — how it should end up, what it needs next, what it will be a year from now — and the deciding has grown heavier than the hands-on part. Whatever grows at this pace gets built before it's shown you what it is, and the shape you've fixed on it stops matching what's actually there. You may have noticed the pleasure thinning out, and pushing a bit harder to get it back.

Here's where the pressure comes off. Sit with one unfinished thing and picture what it could become — no plan attached, nothing to act on, curiosity about something that hasn't happened. Then get up. The imagining is allowed to be idle. It isn't the blueprint, and nothing has to follow from it.
cells.sheetLine: You decide what it becomes before it can show you.
cells.verb: Tending something into the form it is learning to take

cells.tense: Nothing is being reached for and nothing new is being picked up lately.
cells.act: start something for the spark of starting
cells.ask: Begin something tiny and stop at the beginning. No result, nobody depending on it — only the feel of starting. One sitting, then walk away from it and go on.
cells.core:
Things got tended, and that isn't happening now. The hands that learned how form develops are still, and there's a stretch ahead nobody has touched. That is what this capacity does when it's open: it takes hold of a small thing and watches how it grows. Wanting to get going isn't arriving; the days are going somewhere else, and that has become the shape of things.

Holding back from something halfway isn't where this turns. Begin something small — too small to matter, with nothing riding on it and nobody depending on it — and make the starting itself the point. Enthusiasm arrives by moving, not by being mustered first. One beginning, this week, then walk away and go on.

cells.tense: The finishing hand is already at work in a situation nobody is naming as work.
cells.act: bear the duty and know when to let go
cells.ask: Take in hand one duty you are carrying that has already run its course. Put the day you will put it down in your own calendar, and keep that day.
cells.core:
Quietly, without flagging it, you bring things to their end. Around you, things get completed, handed on, let finish properly — and you describe it as if you'd only been keeping up, not as the one who decided when it was done. The author isn't signing. Nobody around you has reason to tell you otherwise, so nobody does.

What came before all this carrying was simpler: you finished something small and stopped. That part is still yours. So take in hand a duty you're holding that has already run its course, put a day on when you'll stand down from it, and keep that day. The call is already yours to make; it just needs a date where the others can see it.
cells.sheetLine: You finish things and call it keeping up. The ending is yours.

attempts.check: The unsupported claim: that the person has built or worked on something before and is now in front of unstarted possibility — the seat says nothing about their history, so all four cores must keep the past out of it and only say what the capacity is doing now. The reader could reasonably say 'I never wanted to make things, I only ever took care of people' — the signature is care learned by hand, so the ask survives that: it is one piece, one tending, one date, one spark, none of which requires them to have ever called themselves a builder. The sentence that serves me more than them is any line that tells them the possibility is precious or that they must not waste it — cut, and the sheet lines stay on what is actually being done or not done.
